representativeSnapshot.kind: Static review of the full staff_performance_metrics policy history in the active chain, plus EXECUTED behavioural evidence on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster. THE DEFECT is real and is a mass-disclosure one: 20250818120000:370-371 (read_all_metrics, SELECT USING auth.role() = 'authenticated'), :404-405 (insert_metrics, INSERT WITH CHECK) and :435-436 (update_metrics, UPDATE USING) are live at chain HEAD. staff_performance_metrics is in NEITHER v_tables array of 20260823210000 (:244-257 and :322-334) and read_all_metrics is not in its v_permissive name list (:259-278), so no sweep in the chain has ever reached this table. The table holds performance_rating, supervisor_rating, customer_feedback_score, attendance_rate, incidents_count, commendations_count and notes. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD AS BRIEFED, BOTH PROVEN BY EXECUTION IN THE HARNESS. (1) The 'correctly scoped policies 20250812093500:41-55 that the permissive policies OR away' do not exist on an ordered replay: that whole DO block is guarded on `if exists (... tablename = 'staff_performance_metrics')` and the table is created six days LATER at 20250818120000:282, which is the only create table staff_performance_metrics in the chain. The harness executes 20250812093500:34-56 verbatim at its own version position and it creates NOTHING; the same block executed again after the table exists creates BOTH policies. That delta is the proof, and it means there is no scoped SELECT policy at all rather than a permissive one nullifying it. (2) The _write text at 20250812093500:49-55 is historical: 20260414120000_security_linter_step3_tighten_rls.sql:26-39 runs after the table exists, drops _write and re-creates it `for all` with the USING mirrored into WITH CHECK, so the one scoped policy live at chain HEAD is the 20260414120000 body. Executed evidence: 76 PASS / 0 FAIL in supabase/tests/db014_staff_performance_metrics_scope.harness.sh, including a real negative control (an authenticated account with no role anywhere reads 4 of 4 performance_rating values across both tenants, INSERTs into venue A and REWRITES venue A's rating BEFORE the migration, and the harness asserts the pre-fix write really landed before restoring the fixture), and the measured denial after it.

assumptions: `public.staff_performance_metrics` has NO `org_id` column. The chain's CREATE TABLE (20250818120000:282-301) and every later reference give `staff_member_id`, `venue_id` (legacy `venues`), `adhoc_venue_id` (`venues_v2`) and `event_id` (`events_v2`) and nothing that names an organization; the harness asserts this against the extracted DDL rather than assuming it. DB-013's `has_perm(uid, org_id, ...)` shape is therefore NOT expressible here without adding a column, which would be a schema change requiring a generated-type change and a backfill. Organization scope for this table is expressed as entity scope over the tenant keys it actually has, through the chain's own `public.has_entity_permission` SECURITY DEFINER (20260823210100:87-129), which is the authority the table's own intended policies used. ROUTED, NOT DECIDED HERE: whether the table should gain an `org_id` (WFC/CP-102 territory) and whether `adhoc_venue_id` should be an authority arm.

`authenticated` holds EXECUTE on `public.has_entity_permission(uuid, text, uuid, text)`. 20260823210100:130-131 grants it to `authenticated` and `20260914090000:17` re-grants it after revoking PUBLIC and anon. The predicates are evaluated as the caller, so this is load-bearing. The chain does not manage function grants uniformly and this is not verifiable from the chain, so it is an operator preflight probe rather than an assumption this lane can discharge. The failure direction is safe: without it the three policies DENY, they never open.

NO TABLE-GRANT DEPENDENCY, unlike DB-013. These three predicates contain no subquery against another table: `has_entity_permission` is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, and the `event_id is not null` guard is evaluated locally. So they do not require `authenticated` to hold table-level SELECT on any other relation. That is a deliberate improvement over the `staff_members` shape and it removes a whole class of false-denial risk.

NO NEW AUTHORITY MECHANISM IS INTRODUCED. The two permissions used are the ones the chain's own text used for this table: `EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS` for read (20250812093500:43) and `ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES` for write (:51). Nothing about who may hold them is changed by this migration.

A row whose `venue_id` AND `event_id` are both NULL becomes invisible to EVERY caller, including a platform admin, and an INSERT with both NULL is rejected. On a fully replayed target such a row was previously readable and writable by every authenticated account, so this is a strict reduction of access and a deliberate narrowing of a state the chain permits. It is the price of the fail-closed rule and is recorded rather than softened. The tenant-key conjunct is redundant against today's `has_entity_permission` (it compares `ur.entity_id = p_entity_id`, NULL can never satisfy a WHERE) and is kept so the guarantee is structural and independently provable rather than an emergent property of another function.

`adhoc_venue_id` is NOT an authority arm. Adding it would WIDEN access inside a security fix, and any widening in a security fix needs its own decision. Consequence, stated: a metrics row whose only tenant key is `adhoc_venue_id` becomes unreachable after this change where before it was reachable by everyone. That is a reduction of the exposure, not a new hole. Routed as a product question in HF-DB-014-EVENT-RESOURCES-AND-CALENDAR-READ-SCOPE.

`staff_performance_metrics_write` (20260414120000:29-37, FOR ALL) is retained and is never dropped or replaced. It is a SCOPED policy and it is the ONLY policy the chain creates that covers DELETE on this table; because policies OR, keeping it makes this migration strictly additive to access. No DELETE policy is added, so delete is neither widened nor narrowed. The migration's post-condition raises a WARNING (not an exception) if no DELETE policy exists on the table at all, so a target whose history differs records the fact instead of having the apply blocked.

`staff_performance_metrics_select` is not created and not reused as a name. On a target where 20250812093500's block actually executed (an out-of-band or reordered apply) that policy is left byte-identical rather than dropped: it is scoped, so it adds nothing to the exposure. The contract test reports it as a DUPLICATE retirement candidate rather than a violation, so the operator sees it instead of being surprised by it.

Every existing `staff_performance_metrics` row is preserved. No table, column, index, constraint, trigger or function is created, altered or dropped; no data row is read for update or deleted. `lib/database.types.ts` is byte-unchanged and this migration requires NO type regeneration, because it changes no table, column or function - only policies. Regeneration is separately blocked (CP-089, CP-092, HF-DB-008-REGENERATION-UNREACHABLE-AND-LINKED-TARGET-IS-A-DIFFERENT-DATABASE) and is not needed here.

`public.event_resources` and `public.event_calendar_items` are NOT in this file. They carry the same CP-104 shape at 20260823221000:36,53 but that migration's own header documents the permissive read as a deliberate contract, and they sit inside DB-002's already-recorded event-HQ surface. They are dispositioned read-only and routed to DB-002; no migration was opened for them.
layeredPlan: Layer 0 (preflight, read-only, operator). Run the Layer 0 queries in preflight.rowCountQueries and record the result. Three things decide whether this file is correct for THIS target: (a) the full policy set on public.staff_performance_metrics with each predicate as PostgreSQL RENDERS it - if a differently-named role-permissive policy is on any of SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE, this migration does not remove it and the operator must stop and route it back rather than improvise an extra drop in the same run; (b) `has_function_privilege('authenticated','public.has_entity_permission(uuid, text, uuid, text)','execute')` - if false, the three new policies deny everything and the intended read path disappears, so stop and report before applying; (c) how many rows have venue_id AND event_id both null, because the post-migration state makes them invisible to every caller and the operator should be able to say out loud whether that is acceptable for this target.

Layer 1 (apply, single run, operator). One transaction, explicit, this file only - never `supabase db reset`, never `db push --include-all`, never a chain replay (CP-051). DROP POLICY IF EXISTS on the three permissive names, DROP+CREATE on each of the three scoped policies, COMMENT ON POLICY on each, then a DO block that RAISEs unless RLS is enabled, the three permissive names are gone, the three scoped policies exist on the right commands, each scoped predicate still carries both its tenant-key conjunct and its permission check, the UPDATE policy gates using and with check with the SAME rendered predicate, no policy on the table carries an unconditional clause, and no policy on the table is reachable by anon or PUBLIC. It RAISEs a WARNING if no DELETE policy exists, which is informational and does not block. The post-condition is inside the same transaction as the change, so a target that cannot reach the asserted state fails the apply rather than reporting success.

Layer 2 (postflight, read-only, operator). Run supabase/tests/db014_staff_performance_metrics_scope_contract.sql; expect zero violation rows and exactly one summary row rendering `DB-014 staff_performance_metrics scope|t`. Then the real-caller probes in postflight.queries, as at least FOUR DIFFERENT identities, because this table has no self-serve read path: a caller with NO role anywhere, a caller holding EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS on the owning venue, a caller holding ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES on the owning venue, and - if the target has any - a caller whose only permission comes from an rbac_user_permission_overrides row. A denial probe run as the wrong identity is not evidence.

Layer 3 (no fourth layer in this lane). Four items the chain leaves open are routed rather than absorbed: the `org_id` question and the `adhoc_venue_id` authority-arm question (both HF-DB-014-EVENT-RESOURCES-AND-CALENDAR-READ-SCOPE), the duplicate `staff_performance_metrics_select` on out-of-band targets, and the fact that no seeded role matrix is changed here. None is required for this migration to be safe, and folding any of them in would widen a security fix into a workforce-identity or product decision it is not sized for.

preflight.expectedAffectedRows: Zero data rows are changed. Three policy names are dropped if present, three policies are created, three comments are set. No table, column, index, constraint, trigger or function is created, altered or dropped. No DELETE policy is added, so delete coverage is unchanged.

execution.resumeStrategy: Authored - manual apply pending (CP-051). One transaction, one file. DROP POLICY and CREATE POLICY take locks on catalog rows, not on the table's data, and no table is rewritten or re-vacuumed, so there is no lock-budget risk from the data side. Safe to apply BEFORE any consumer change: because RLS policies are permissive and OR, and because staff_performance_metrics_write is retained, no committed surface loses a row it could previously read, insert, update or delete. The only behaviour that changes is that a caller with no scope on a venue or event can no longer read, insert or update that tenant's rows - which is the point of the change. The only ACCESS THAT DISAPPEARS for a legitimate caller is the read path of someone holding neither EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS nor ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES on the row's venue or event; that path did not exist as a deliberate grant, it existed as the bug.
execution.idempotency: Deterministic and repeatable. DROP POLICY IF EXISTS on the three permissive names; DROP POLICY IF EXISTS + CREATE POLICY with a final name on each of the three scoped policies; COMMENT ON POLICY; a DO block that only reads the catalog and RAISEs or WARNINGs. Verified by applying the file twice on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster in supabase/tests/db014_staff_performance_metrics_scope.harness.sh: the second apply produced no error and the surviving policy set was byte-identical, measured as staff_performance_metrics_scoped_insert,staff_performance_metrics_scoped_read,staff_performance_metrics_scoped_update,staff_performance_metrics_write before and after.

quarantine.strategy: No data movement, no backfill, no batch. The change is six policy objects. There is no partial-application state: the file is one transaction and its own post-condition RAISEs if the asserted state is unreachable, so a half-applied policy set cannot be committed.
quarantine.lockBudget: `has_entity_permission` is wrapped in `(select ...)` so the planner evaluates the SECURITY DEFINER call as an InitPlan once per statement rather than once per row. Its own body is three indexed lookups on rbac_user_entity_roles / rbac_role_permissions / rbac_permissions / rbac_user_permission_overrides, all of which carry indexes from 20250812090000:66-75. The read path is served by idx_staff_metrics_venue_date (20250818120000:303) on (venue_id, metric_date desc), which is a prefix match for the venue arm. The tenant-key conjunct is a local NULL test on two columns already loaded with the row, so it costs nothing at plan time. The added work versus the pre-existing scoped policy is the InitPlan wrapper, which removes per-row evaluation rather than adding it.

constraints: No constraint is added, altered or dropped. staff_performance_metrics_venue_id_fkey, staff_performance_metrics_adhoc_venue_id_fkey, staff_performance_metrics_event_id_fkey and staff_performance_metrics_staff_member_id_fkey are untouched.

The three new policies ARE the authorization boundary. staff_performance_metrics_scoped_read requires (venue_id is not null or event_id is not null) AND (EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS on the row's venue, or on its event when it has one). staff_performance_metrics_scoped_insert and _update require the same shape with ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES. _update gates BOTH using and with check with the identical rendered predicate, so a caller who may score one venue cannot re-scope a row onto another venue or event, and cannot strip a row's tenant entirely.

staff_performance_metrics_write (20260414120000:29-37) is NOT dropped. It is scoped, and it is the only DELETE coverage the chain creates for this table, so dropping it would remove access rather than add it. The contract test's check 8 allow-lists it by name so that any THIRD survivor is reported rather than assumed benign.
No DELETE policy is added. Delete is therefore neither widened nor narrowed by this file.
indexes: No index is added. The new policies add no new access pattern: the venue arm's InitPlan performs a rbac_user_entity_roles lookup that the pre-existing staff_performance_metrics_write policy already performed on the same rows, and the event arm likewise.
constraintsAndIndexes.validationPlan: supabase/tests/db014_staff_performance_metrics_scope_contract.sql returns violation rows only, plus one summary row `DB-014 staff_performance_metrics scope|t` computed from the same predicates, so an unapplied target cannot pass vacuously. It asserts 9 properties: RLS enabled; the three permissive names absent; no policy on the table carries an unconditional USING or WITH CHECK for a command that takes one, branching on polcmd so a FOR INSERT policy's structurally-absent USING is not reported; no policy on the table is reachable by anon or PUBLIC; the three scoped policies exist on the right command scoped to authenticated; each scoped predicate still carries BOTH its tenant-key conjunct and its permission check for the right command; the UPDATE policy's using and with check are the SAME rendered predicate; any surviving policy beyond the four known names is reported; and no sweep-exempt-named policy on the table is role-permissive. The predicates are matched as PostgreSQL RENDERS them, not as they were written, because matching the source spelling fails against a healthy target. The behavioural half is supabase/tests/db014_staff_performance_metrics_scope.harness.sh, which first proves the chain-HEAD policy set by executing the chain's own guarded blocks at their own version positions, measures the cross-tenant read/insert/update/delete BEFORE the migration as a negative control, measures them after, proves a tenant-less row is invisible to five distinct callers including one whose permission comes from an override, proves the new read path GRANTS on both the venue and the event arm, proves DELETE coverage is unchanged, then removes a policy and confirms the postflight reports it, then re-introduces read_all_metrics ALONGSIDE the scoped policy and confirms the postflight still reports it, then strips the tenant-key conjunct and confirms the postflight reports THAT too, then re-applies and confirms green.

recovery.rollback: DROP POLICY staff_performance_metrics_scoped_read ON public.staff_performance_metrics; DROP POLICY staff_performance_metrics_scoped_insert ON public.staff_performance_metrics; DROP POLICY staff_performance_metrics_scoped_update ON public.staff_performance_metrics; - issued as a later forward migration, never as an edit to this file. Rolling back does NOT re-open the exposure on a fully replayed target, because 20250818120000's three permissive policies are still there and this migration is the only thing that removed them; a rollback therefore DOES re-open the cross-tenant exposure, which is why the preferred recovery for a bad apply is a forward fix, not this rollback.
recovery.forwardFix: Any correction is a new additive migration with a higher version carrying DROP/CREATE POLICY for public.staff_performance_metrics. The post-state DO block in this file will raise on such a migration's own apply if it leaves an unconditional clause or an anon/PUBLIC-reachable policy behind, so a bad forward fix cannot be applied silently. Note that a forward fix cannot accidentally inherit a name the 20260823210000 sweep exempts, because this file's policies are named staff_performance_metrics_scoped_* and match none of the six exemption patterns; supabase/tests/db014_sweep_exemption_permissive_policies.sql asserts that on a real target, and the new DB-014 detector check would fail if the chain's exemption list ever grew to cover them.

-- A CORRECT DENIAL LOOKS LIKE THIS. Run each as a real caller with that caller's own JWT; label the result with WHICH identity ran it. (1) cross-tenant read, an account with NO rbac role and no override anywhere: SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_performance_metrics; -> returns 0. The query SUCCEEDS. 0 rows, not a permission error: the role still holds the table grant and RLS is what filters the rows. An `ERROR: permission denied for table` here means the GRANT is missing, which is a different problem and not a pass.

-- (2) cross-tenant read of the sensitive column specifically, same account: SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_performance_metrics WHERE performance_rating IS NOT NULL; -> returns 0. This is the probe that matches the finding, and it is the one to attach to the release ticket.

-- (3) cross-tenant insert, same account: INSERT INTO public.staff_performance_metrics (venue_id, metric_date, performance_rating) VALUES ('<other venue uuid>', current_date, 0); -> ERROR 42501: new row violates row-level security policy for table "staff_performance_metrics". That exact error is the correct outcome. INSERT 0 1, or success of any kind, is a FAILURE and means the exposure is still open.

-- (4) cross-tenant update, same account: UPDATE public.staff_performance_metrics SET performance_rating = 0 WHERE id = '<a row id in the other venue>'; -> UPDATE 0. Then SELECT performance_rating FROM public.staff_performance_metrics WHERE id = '<that id>'; -> unchanged. UPDATE 1 is a FAILURE.

-- (5) NON-REGRESSION, a caller holding EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS on the owning venue: SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_performance_metrics; -> returns that venue's row count, NOT 0. This probe is the one most likely to be forgotten and it is the one this migration can break: the chain never actually created the scoped SELECT policy, so before this migration an EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS-only holder's read existed only because of the bug. If this returns 0, the apply has OVER-denied and must be rolled forward, not accepted.

-- (6) NON-REGRESSION, a caller holding ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES on the owning venue: SELECT ...; -> that venue's row count, and DELETE FROM public.staff_performance_metrics WHERE id = '<a probe row>' -> DELETE 1. That delete is served by the RETAINED staff_performance_metrics_write policy; if it returns DELETE 0, delete coverage was lost and this migration is not the cause to fix - it is the signal to stop and report.

-- (7) fail-closed probe, as ANY caller: SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_performance_metrics WHERE venue_id IS NULL AND event_id IS NULL; -> 0. A row that names no tenant is invisible to everyone after this migration, including a platform admin. If the Layer 0 count of such rows was non-zero, report that number in the release ticket rather than treating 0 as automatically correct.

-- (8) fail-closed probe on write, as a caller who genuinely holds ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES on a venue: INSERT INTO public.staff_performance_metrics (venue_id, event_id, metric_date, performance_rating) VALUES (NULL, NULL, current_date, 1); -> ERROR 42501. This must fail even for a legitimate caller, or the fail-closed rule is a permission accident rather than a rule.
SELECT count(*) AS metric_rows, count(*) FILTER (WHERE venue_id IS NULL AND event_id IS NULL) AS tenantless_rows FROM public.staff_performance_metrics

evidence: supabase/tests/db014_staff_performance_metrics_scope.harness.sh - EXECUTED, ALL CHECKS PASSED, 76 PASS / 0 FAIL, exit 0, on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster.

THE FINDING IS PROVEN BY EXECUTION, NOT BY READING. The harness extracts the chain's own 20250812093500:34-56 block, runs it at that migration's own version position on a database where staff_performance_metrics does not exist, and asserts it created NOTHING. It then creates the table from the chain's own 20250818120000:282-301 DDL, runs the SAME block again, and asserts it created BOTH policies. That 0 -> 2 delta is the guard-ordering defect, measured, with a control that rules out 'the block is dead code'.

The chain-HEAD policy set is then reproduced and asserted as a single string: insert_metrics,read_all_metrics,staff_performance_metrics_write,update_metrics. There is NO scoped SELECT policy. The harness additionally asserts that _write's WITH CHECK is the 20260414120000 mirrored body and not the 20250812093500 `with check (true)`, which is the second correction.

The negative control is real, not assumed. With that policy set in place, an authenticated account with no rbac role and no override anywhere: reads 4 distinct performance_rating values across both tenants; reads venue B's exact rating (1.0) by id; INSERTs a metrics row into venue A; REWRITES venue A's rating; and the harness asserts the write really landed (ROW_A.performance_rating = 0.0) before restoring the fixture. Without that, the after-state would measure nothing.

After the migration, the same account: reads 0 of 4 rows; reads 0 performance_rating values; a targeted read of venue B's row returns an empty result, not an error; INSERT is rejected with `new row violates row-level security policy for table "staff_performance_metrics"`; UPDATE matches 0 rows; DELETE matches 0 rows; venue A's rating is unchanged at 4.5.

WITH CHECK is proven independently of USING: a venue A manager who CAN read the row is REJECTED re-scoping it onto venue B, and separately REJECTED stripping its tenant entirely. Both are ERROR 42501 and both leave the row byte-unchanged.

Fail-closed is proven for five distinct callers: the no-role attacker, a venue-A viewer, a venue-A manager, an override-holder on venue B, and an event-A viewer. None can read the tenant-less row. The denial is non-vacuous because the harness FIRST asserts that the override holder's permission genuinely works - it reads venue B's row - and that has_entity_permission on a NULL entity id is false, and that a venue-only permission does NOT read the event-keyed row.

The new read path is proven to GRANT on BOTH arms and to be necessary. The harness asserts staff_performance_metrics_select does not exist before measuring any read, so the reads that follow can only have come from staff_performance_metrics_scoped_read. A venue-scoped EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS holder reads venue A's row and NOT the event-keyed row; an event-scoped holder reads the event-keyed row and NOT the venue-keyed row. The two arms are independent, and a viewer's UPDATE matches 0 rows and INSERT is rejected, so EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS is not ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES and the new read is read-only.

Non-regression is proven on both surviving paths: an ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES holder still reads, still updates (4.5 -> 4.0, asserted landed), still DELETES, and still INSERTS into their own venue, through the untouched staff_performance_metrics_write. Delete coverage is therefore provably unchanged, which is the claim the migration header makes.

The postflight is proven able to fail THREE times, in the three ways that matter: once by removing staff_performance_metrics_scoped_read; once by re-introducing read_all_metrics WHILE the scoped policy is present (the CP-104 case a scoped-successor check scores as safe); and once by stripping the tenant-key conjunct from the read policy, leaving a policy that only fails closed because of has_entity_permission's NULL arithmetic. Re-applying the migration returns the postflight to green each time.
Idempotency: applied twice with no error, policy set compared byte-identical before and after.

The harness asserts its own pre-state (4 policies, exactly the chain-HEAD set; 4 rows; 10 asserted has_entity_permission preconditions) and its own post-state (the exact 4-name surviving policy set, and 0 rows for a cross-tenant caller). It also HARD-ABORTS if any fixture-stage check fails rather than continuing: a silently failed fixture is the Wave 33 failure shape, and the first revision of this harness did produce exactly that noise (48 downstream FAILs from a one-line extraction error) until the bail was added.

TWO DEFECTS IN THIS LANE'S OWN WORK WERE FOUND BY ITS OWN GATES, both recorded because they are the reusable lesson. (a) The migration's first post-condition raised on a HEALTHY target: it inspected pg_policies-style quals for the FOR INSERT policy, whose USING is structurally absent. That is precisely the polcmd confusion DB-013 documented, reintroduced in the same repository three hours later, and the harness caught it on the first apply. A policy DDL check must branch on polcmd before deciding which clause is expected to be NULL. (b) The detector's scoped-construct list initially contained a bare `role`, which matches inside `auth.role()` - the exact construct the detector exists to catch. Three fixture cases that must have fired came back clean. A construct list that cannot see its own target is worse than a short one.

LOCAL EMULATION ONLY: PostgreSQL 16.15, a throwaway cluster in a temp dir, the shared db011 auth/roles bootstrap, and chain CREATE TABLE / DO-block / function text extracted verbatim by line range. Not Supabase, not a hosted project, not a chain replay, no `supabase db reset`, no `db push --include-all` (CP-051).

NOT PROVEN HERE and required before this is launch-grade: behaviour on a real Supabase target; whether `authenticated` actually holds EXECUTE on has_entity_permission there; PostgREST schema-cache refresh; whether the three permissive policies are present or absent on any given target (DB-002's out-of-band Management API application means the chain cannot answer that, and it is the single largest reason this file is worth applying rather than declaring the finding closed); whether any consumer reads or writes staff_performance_metrics through a path this change would alter; and how many tenant-less rows a given target actually holds, which decides whether the fail-closed rule is a clean deny or a functional change that needs an owner.
